learningObjective: Compare where sigmoid, ReLU, and exact GELU flatten so the connection between output shape and gradient flow is visible.
mediumRationale: Two deterministic SVG plots are the smallest medium that can show numeric axes, asymptotes, the ReLU dead half-line, and GELU's smooth negative shoulder together. Mermaid cannot express function shape; semantic HTML is unsuitable for continuous curves; interaction adds no necessary inference; source-figure reuse creates avoidable provenance risk; and prose alone makes the flat regions difficult to compare.

pages.insight: The preceding section divider introduces general neural-network concepts but contains no activation details.
The activation slide identifies sigmoid saturation, ReLU's dying-unit region, leaky ReLU, and GELU approximations.
The following learning divider adds no activation-function behavior.
The next gradient-descent section connects activation slopes to optimization but adds no comparative curves.

deckReview.notes: Pages 40 through 43 of the 214-page Basic_ML_CS_concepts deck were inspected directly. Page 41's claim that GELU is self-normalizing and its labeling of x sigmoid(1.702x) as GELU were not adopted. The site plot uses the exact definition x times the standard normal CDF and original coordinates.

sourceReview.notes: All plotted values are original deterministic samples of sigmoid, ReLU, and exact GELU over labeled domains. Sigmoid and tanh were reviewed as saturating functions; ReLU, leaky ReLU, ELU, GELU, and SiLU derivative behavior was checked to ensure the article and focused comparison do not claim gradients are nonzero everywhere.

agentReview.summary: Reviewed the complete article, deck pages 40-43, and authoritative activation definitions. Recommended two small plots focused on gradient-flow consequences instead of a gallery of every activation.

implementation.accessibility: The SVGs include separate titles and complete descriptions. Numeric axes, direct curve labels, explicit saturation and dead-region annotations, solid versus dashed strokes, and the caption preserve the comparison without relying on color. The authored trace adds exact output and slope tables at x=-2, x=0, and x=2, keyboard stepping, and print-visible states.

mechanismTrace.contract: Static first state, keyboard and playback stepping, reduced-motion single-step behavior, stable function-row keys, and print-visible authored states.
